### Stack & Responsibilities
- Software Engineer building backend services, APIs, and Vue applications for Coursedog’s academic operations platform. Delivering scalable features that help colleges and universities improve student success.
Software Engineer building Coursedog’s academic operations platform for colleges and universities
- Salary: $70,000 - $90,000 per year
- Tech stack: AWS, Java, JavaScript, MongoDB, Node.js, Python, Redis, TypeScript, Vue.js, .NET
- Visa sponsorship signal: company profile says it sponsors H1B visas. Treat as a small scoring bonus, not a guarantee for this role.
- Build and maintain backend services and APIs
- Develop and maintain frontend applications using TypeScript and Vue or similar frameworks
- Design, implement, and maintain well-structured, testable code
- Review pull requests and provide constructive, actionable feedback
- Debug, refactor, and improve existing systems, including legacy components
- Use AI tools across coding, debugging, and documentation

- Establish and document engineering best practices for the team

- Experience building frontend applications with Vue.js or a similar framework
- Experience developing backend services with Node.js
- Knowledge of REST APIs and software design principles
- Experience with MongoDB, Redis, and relational databases
- Strong debugging and problem-solving skills

### Full Job Description
Summary:
Software Engineer building backend services, APIs, and Vue applications for Coursedog’s academic operations platform. Delivering scalable features that help colleges and universities improve student success.
Software Engineer building Coursedog’s academic operations platform for colleges and universities
Role description:
• Build and maintain backend services and APIs
• Develop and maintain frontend applications using TypeScript and Vue or similar frameworks
• Design, implement, and maintain well-structured, testable code
• Review pull requests and provide constructive, actionable feedback
• Debug, refactor, and improve existing systems, including legacy components
• Use AI tools across coding, debugging, and documentation
• Collaborate with cross-functional partners to deliver features and resolve issues
• Establish and document engineering best practices for the team
• Own problems from scoping through release, including new development and system improvements
Role requirements:
• Experience writing TypeScript and modern JavaScript in production applications
• Experience building frontend applications with Vue.js or a similar framework
• Experience developing backend services with Node.js
• Knowledge of REST APIs and software design principles
• Experience with MongoDB, Redis, and relational databases
• Strong debugging and problem-solving skills
• Ability to learn new systems quickly in ambiguous problem spaces
• Strong communication skills with technical and non-technical partners
• Experience using AI tools to speed up development while maintaining code quality
• Nice to have: experience with AWS, queues, or serverless systems such as Lambda
• Nice to have: exposure to AI-powered or AI-adjacent systems
• Nice to have: backend experience beyond Node.js, such as Python, Java, or .NET
Benefits:
• Healthcare, dental, and vision coverage through Aetna and Guardian
• Spring Health mental health support
• XP Health vision benefits
• Carrot Fertility family planning support
• One Medical primary care
• Health Savings Accounts (HSA)
• Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
• Safe Harbor 401(k) plan from day one
• 4% employer match on total compensation, subject to federal limits
• Unlimited Paid Time Off
• Remote-first work flexibility
• Equity grants aligned to role and tenure
• Equity grants reviewed and adjusted with promotions
• Up to 6 weeks of Paid Bonding Leave at 100% of base pay for all parents
• Birthing parents receive an additional 6 weeks of Paid Medical Recovery Leave at 100% of base pay, up to 12 weeks total
Tech stack:
AWS, Java, JavaScript, MongoDB, Node.js, Python, Redis, TypeScript, Vue.js, .NET
Company sponsorship flag: sponsorsH1B=true.
